key_insight: Automated model discovery identified a sparse three-term hyperelastic law for TPU-coated woven nylon, combining one isotropic and two anisotropic contributions.
engineering_relevance: The discovered law can support finite-element simulations of fabric-based structures, including soft robotic devices.
method: Fit Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks to biaxial test data.
Discover constitutive terms and calibrate their parameters simultaneously.
Compare with independent sparse regression using LARS-LASSO.
evidence_signal: The neural-network models reproduced measured biaxial responses with mean R² = 0.97 and robust accuracy across 20 initializations; LARS-LASSO recovered the same dominant contributions at approximately 100-fold lower computational cost.
watch_item: Correlated candidate terms yield different sparse representations with similar accuracy, so predictive fit alone does not establish a unique constitutive law.
paper_title: Unweaving the mechanics of woven fabrics through automated model discovery
